headline: Banks are earning their yield this results season, but a softer rupee and a third straight week of falling reserves keep the desk from calling this a clean risk-on tape.
summary: PSX sits in a neutral-to-cautious spot: global markets are calm (VIX near 15.6, US stocks firm, oil off its highs though still up double digits this month), but the rupee softened 0.8% today to 277.7 and reserves have now fallen three straight weeks to $17.03bn after Pakistan posted a rare FY26 current-account deficit. July inflation eased sharply to 9.2%, partly a base-effect story, and SBP held rates at 11.5%. Bank earnings season is delivering real beats (BAFL, AKBL both up double-digits), which is why the desk leans toward quality yield names and stays wary of import-heavy, high-beta names until the currency stabilizes.

sectors.name: Commercial Banks
sectors.why: T-bill (11.79%) and PIB (12.14%) yields still sit well above the held 11.5% policy rate, and Q2 results are beating — BAFL profit +27% YoY, AKBL +25% YoY per the latest prints.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas Exploration (E&P)
sectors.why: Brent is still up 13.2% over the past month even after today's pullback, which is a direct tailwind for OGDC/PPL/MARI-type earnings.

sectors.name: OMCs & Refineries
sectors.why: Daily fuel-price revisions plus a fragile external account (reserves down three straight weeks) make margin timing risky for ATRL/NRL/PRL/Cnergyico, even with deregulation being discussed.

sectors.name: Textiles & Exporters
sectors.why: FY26 closed with exports up just 0.2% against imports up 8.5%, the exact mix that produced the current-account deficit — no sign yet of that reversing.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Maple Leaf's FY26 profit was up 9% YoY, a steady but unspectacular number, and the sector still carries fuel/energy cost pressure per the desk's risk radar.

sectors.name: Fertiliser
sectors.why: Easing Brent helps input costs, but the sector's dividend safety is uneven — EFERT's payout ratio is a stretched 93% against FFC's healthier 63%.

watchlist.angle: The volume-leads-price setup (obv_divergence_up) is live on BML today — on its own 89-trade history it has won 96.6% of the time for an average net gain of 5.1%, and it's still holding up out-of-sample (83.3%), the desk's highest-confidence trigger right now. Fundamentals back it up: BML screens 'attractive' with a cheap P/E of 6.4 against a 32% net margin, and results are pencilled in for 2026-08-07 (date unconfirmed) — right in the middle of a bank results season where peers have been beating. Its sector, Commercial Banks, is also the one sector the macro backdrop explicitly favours today.
watchlist.risk: Pays no dividend to cushion a miss, and at a Rs58.8bn mid-cap size, thinner liquidity can exaggerate any post-results swing in either direction.

watchlist.angle: A triple-screen trend setup triggered on ATLH — 75% win rate over 20 historical trades, and it held up perfectly out-of-sample (100%), though the small sample keeps the desk's confidence at 'medium' rather than 'high.' Fundamentals are 'mixed' (P/E 9.06, fair) but the dividend is real and covered: a 6.84% yield on just a 36% payout.
watchlist.risk: No dated earnings catalyst currently on the desk's calendar for ATLH — the case rests on the technical trigger and the yield alone until fresh numbers land.

watchlist.angle: No fresh technical trigger today, but BAFL just posted a genuine Q2 beat — profit up 27% YoY to roughly Rs10bn (EPS 3.22), confirmed across independent sources — on top of an 'attractive' fundamental score (P/E 5.46, 10.23% dividend yield on a well-covered 43% payout). It goes ex-dividend 2026-08-12 (book closure 2026-08-13) paying Rs3/share, a confirmed, dated catalyst, and Banks remain the sector the macro backdrop is leaning toward.
watchlist.risk: Its own strategy-map backtest sample (a golden-cross setup) is thin, only 12 trades, so this pick leans on fundamentals and the confirmed dividend date rather than a fresh technical signal — a soft market reaction around the ex-dividend date would undercut the thesis.

catalysts.event: NESTLE book closure (dividend Rs213/share, ~2.74% yield) — confirmed
SBP weekly FX reserves print — watched for whether the third straight weekly decline (to $17.03bn) extends
SBP FY27 Monetary Policy Report release
FFC and EFERT book closures (dividends Rs14.5 and Rs1.75/share respectively) — confirmed
BAFL and AKBL go ex-dividend (Rs3.0 and Rs2.0/share) ahead of 2026-08-13 book closures — confirmed
SBP MPC — second FY27 monetary policy decision

risks: The rupee has now weakened for a stretch running into the 2026-08-07 reserves print — a fourth straight weekly decline would harden the case that SBP stays cautious through the 2026-09-14 MPC, a headwind for import-heavy names.

Pakistan's FY26 current account flipped into a $139mn deficit as imports (+8.5%) outran exports (+0.2%) despite record remittances — the external account is fragile, not fixed, and any further import surge would pressure the currency.

The desk's conflict/escalation risk factor is still pinned at maximum stress (100/100) even though recent headlines have calmed — a re-flare in the Iran/Gulf situation would hit oil-sensitive PSX sectors (OMCs, cement) fast, per the sector-pressure read.
